children: The Kansas City Fed’s Manufacturing Production Index rose to 20 in September 2026, its highest reading since April 2022, up from 17 in the previous month.
Both durable and nondurable manufacturing activity increased, driven primarily by plastics and rubber products and furniture-related products.
Monthly activity was broadly stronger, with shipments increasing to 21 from 17, while the volume of new orders rose to 24 from 16, both a multi-month high.
Employment was flat for a second consecutive month.
Price pressures also intensified, particularly for raw materials.
Compared with a year earlier, the manufacturing production index eased slightly to 19, while shipments increased to 23 from 13 and the volume of new orders fell to 22 from 23.
Price pressures also increased further, while employment declined to -3 from 5.
Over the next six months, activity is expected to remain in expansionary territory, although the index edged down to 9 from 20.

title: Kansas Fed Manufacturing Activity Rises in September
